title: Information Technology Act, 2000
summary: India's principal statute addressing electronic records, digital signatures and specified cyber offences.
points: Recognises electronic records and electronic signatures within the legal framework.
Contains provisions dealing with offences such as identity theft, cheating by personation using computer resources, and violation of privacy.
Section 43A was omitted by the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023; avoid relying on outdated summaries that present it as a current operative provision.
The Act is not a complete substitute for understanding other criminal, consumer, data-protection and constitutional laws.
tip: For a real incident, preserve evidence and seek advice from a qualified professional.

title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
summary: A framework concerning processing of digital personal data and the responsibilities of Data Fiduciaries.
points: The Act uses concepts including Data Principal (the individual the data relates to) and Data Fiduciary (the entity deciding why and how data is processed).
It provides for notice, consent in applicable cases, certain individual rights, duties and grievance mechanisms, subject to the Act and rules.
The precise commencement and implementation of provisions depend on official notifications and rules. Check the latest Gazette and MeitY material before relying on a specific duty or deadline.
This learning portal is educational and does not provide legal advice.
tip: Read privacy notices before sharing personal information; share only what is needed.

title: Constitutional digital rights
summary: Constitutional protections remain relevant when people use digital services and communicate online.
points: Article 19(1)(a) protects freedom of speech and expression, subject to the reasonable restrictions in Article 19(2).
Article 21 protects life and personal liberty; the Supreme Court recognised privacy as a fundamental right in the Puttaswamy judgment (2017).
Rights online are not unlimited: lawful restrictions and the rights of others also matter.
A platform's terms of service are different from constitutional rights and statutory protections.
tip: Think before posting: lawful expression does not include a licence to threaten, defame or harass others.

title: Common cyber offences
summary: Recognise common forms of online harm and know where to seek help.
points: Phishing: deceptive messages or websites designed to obtain credentials or financial information.
Identity theft and impersonation: misuse of another person's identifying information or credentials.
Cyberstalking, threats, harassment and non-consensual sharing of intimate material can have serious legal consequences.
Online financial fraud should be reported promptly to the bank/payment provider and the official cybercrime reporting system.
tip: Never share an OTP, UPI PIN, password or screen-sharing access with someone who contacts you unexpectedly.

title: Platforms and intermediary rules
summary: Intermediaries have legal obligations under Indian law, including applicable due-diligence requirements.
points: The Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, as amended, set due-diligence requirements for intermediaries.
Platforms may provide grievance channels; check the platform's current grievance policy and official contact route.
A platform report does not replace a police complaint or other legal remedy where one is appropriate.
Do not assume every post is automatically removed: processes depend on the law, facts and applicable procedure.
tip: Save the post URL, account details, date/time and relevant messages before reporting, if safe to do so.

title: Copyright and digital content
summary: Digital content is not automatically free to copy simply because it is easy to download or share.
points: The Copyright Act, 1957 protects qualifying original literary, dramatic, musical and artistic works, films and sound recordings.
Permission, licence terms, public-domain status and statutory exceptions determine whether a use is lawful.
Give attribution where required, but remember that credit alone does not replace permission.
Use openly licensed or public-domain material and follow the licence conditions.
tip: Before reusing an image, video, code sample or song, check its licence and permitted uses.
